source: The 2026-11-18 navego.pages.dev rebrand and consistency pass: logo, wordmark, eyebrows, type and spacing system, nav notch, copy pass. User direction arrived 2026-11-18; internet sources were verified 2026-11-18. Repo sources point at the docs that already carry the decision. 2026-11-19: a source-backed pass over the agent tool surface added D55-D68 - kind recorded carries the file:line of the recorded performance, per the user evidence mandate.
note: One decision, one source. Code references this file as decisions.json -> <id>. A decision added from 2026-11-19 onward carries a file-based id (for example local-canvas-01) and names the file it governs; the earlier D-numbers are history and keep their ids. A decision the user asked for carries kind=user; a decision nobody asked for carries the internet source it was taken from; a decision inherited from this repo carries the repo document that already carries it; a decision taken because a recorded performance demanded it carries kind=recorded with the file:line that records it.

decisions.decision: One idea per tile, headline of 2-6 words; the supporting line is one sentence; nothing advertises more than one benefit at a time.

source.ref: https://www.apple.com (product tiles: one idea per headline); https://developer.apple.com/app-store/product-page/ (concise informative paragraph); https://marketingexamined.com/blog/how-to-write-copy-like-apple (one big idea per headline; inverted pyramid)

decisions.decision: Sentences stay short and carry one idea each; paragraphs stay short enough to scan, written for a reader who skims before reading.

source.ref: https://marketingexamined.com/blog/how-to-write-copy-like-apple (Apple copy uses short paragraphs, short sentences and simple words; write for scanners)

decisions.decision: Address the reader in the second person, in the present tense, with verbs that are things the product literally does (read, fill, click, save); no adjectives praising the product, no exclamation marks.

source.ref: https://help.apple.com/pdf/applestyleguide/en_US/apple-style-guide.pdf (Apple style guide: sentence-style headings, second person, active voice); https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2022/10037/ (write like a person, one idea at a time)

decisions.decision: Inverted pyramid in every section: the claim first, the strongest proof second, the rest last - readers who stop after one line still leave with the right idea.

source.ref: https://marketingexamined.com/blog/how-to-write-copy-like-apple (big headlines showcase one idea, inverted-pyramid paragraphs: biggest benefit to smallest); https://linear.app (claim, then proof, then link)

source.ref: https://www.apple.com (product demos ship the interface as the marketing); https://linear.app (the product UI as the marketing); https://www.raycast.com/ (typewriter prompt panel as the hero)

source.also: https://www.anthropic.com/research/writing-tools-for-agents - pagination, range selection, filtering and truncation for tool responses; the 25,000-token default; redundant tool calls suggest rightsizing pagination or token limits

source.also: https://www.anthropic.com/research/writing-tools-for-agents - too many or overlapping tools distract agents from efficient strategies; consolidate functionality into tools with a clear, distinct purpose

decisions.decision: browser_find_text folds into browser_find_element as mode text: one locate tool, two modalities - role+name resolves a centred anti-stale handle; a plain text resolves viewport rects in the same space a screenshot uses; the handle is the only click currency.

source.ref: catalog descriptions of 2026-11-19: find_element returns the handle and box, measured from the node at the click; find_text returns each match with a viewport rect in the same space a screenshot uses - one page, two lookups, overlapping purpose
source.also: https://www.anthropic.com/research/writing-tools-for-agents - tools should have a clear, distinct purpose; overlapping tools distract

source.also: catalog measurement 2026-11-19 (45 tools): descriptions sum to 3,877 words, 21,159 characters

decisions.decision: The log is read with navego failures (counts by tool and code, the recent failures, every note) and never leaves the machine; the owner machine is the sink, not a server; deleting the file is always safe - it is an observation channel, not a ledger.

decisions.decision: The calling agent leaves the suggestion behind with navego feedback <tool> <note> - one append-only line tied to the tool, surfaced beside the failure counts; that is how an agent that uses a tool and sees it break leaves the fix idea where the maintainer will find it without a server round trip.

Nothing is ever brought to the foreground (D73).

source.ref: owner console capture 2026-11-24: the Supabase oauth consent screen answered 400 unauthorized request origin for the live domain; CI read run 45373897531 printed site_url=https://opera-agent.pages.dev; patch runs 45373987185 and 45376655642 moved it to https://navego.pages.dev and added https://navego.pages.dev/* to uri_allow_list (verified in run logs)

decisions.decision: The database owns the PayPal order lifecycle: the quote is stored when PayPal creates the order, the completed order is compared with that quote, one environment and order id can write one revenue event, and only the activation RPC can change the plan. The capture path and the verified webhook therefore leave one sale and one activation even when both arrive; an APPROVED order is not revenue.

source.ref: user 2026-11-24: 'setiap ada kenaikan saldo adalah kemenangan naik point ... setiap saldo naik 1 dollar dihitung satu point' - real settled revenue must be visible before the agent scores a balance or a paid plan
source.also: live production query 2026-11-24: opera_price_orders held 0 rows, opera_notification_log held only Midtrans sandbox events, and opera_plan_activate_purchase changed plans without recording a PayPal settlement; tests/hosted/paypal-settlement.test.ts, tests/hosted/integration-postgres.test.ts, tests/billing/paypal.test.ts, and tests/billing/paypal-wiring.test.ts

decisions.decision: A PayPal settlement keeps quoted and actual owner/plan values apart, normalizes the environment and order id before taking its lock, derives an unknown order from the insert result, and permits one accepted PayPal revenue event per environment and order id. Malformed actual values therefore enter review without breaking the revenue record, and equivalent keys cannot race into two sales.

source.ref: user 2026-11-24: 'setiap ada kenaikan saldo adalah kemenangan naik point ... turun saldo setiap 1 dollar dihitung - 1 poin' - a real payment must remain visible and count once even when the buyer return and the provider webhook arrive together
source.also: independent review 2026-11-25 after PR #442 found that raw advisory-lock keys and constrained actual values could hide or duplicate a malformed payment; tests/hosted/paypal-settlement-hardening.test.ts and tests/hosted/integration-postgres.test.ts

decisions.decision: Every USD plan carries one canonical price in cents. The billing function refuses an active price row that differs from that map before PayPal is asked for money, and the site-price test keeps the displayed price aligned with the same number.

source.also: tests/billing/plans.test.ts and tests/billing/paypal-wiring.test.ts

decisions.decision: The download hero leads with the Windows one-command install and keeps manual zip and reg installs as secondary paths. A successful command copy invokes the install tracker, while copy failure is visible and announced; the copy control stays enabled, every command owns one polite status region, a successful result is not hidden by a later failure, and the copy controller invalidates work that resolves after disposal.

source.ref: docs/agent-survival-prompt.md:61 (fix the earliest real funnel drop-off, which may be the install path); live production funnel 2026-11-25 had 109 page views, 49 pair views, 2 install views, 0 install clicks, and 0 settled orders
source.also: tests/site/install-cta.test.ts, tests/site/copy-command.test.ts, and the independent 320px browser review on 2026-11-25

decisions.decision: The anonymous landing hero carries the same exact Windows one-command install as the download page, so a visitor can start installation without a second page. The force-install cost and undo path appear before the control; the copy remains retryable and announced; the landing surface records its own view and successful-copy intent with surface=landing, while manual macOS and Linux installation stays linked.

source.ref: hourly survival-and-growth run #5 on 2026-11-25: live production had 62 landing-page views from 60 browsers but only 5 download-page views from 2 browsers and 0 install clicks; fix the earliest measured arrival-to-install gap without weakening the checkout or payment path
source.also: tests/site/install-command.test.ts, tests/site/install-cta.test.ts, and the 320px built-site browser proof on 2026-11-25
